<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**24** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **8** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/ai.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/ai.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **8** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/ai.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/ai.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ad632a23a8cadbe8cfae8f1c3fee1052defada29` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1ec515b6b1d6e773119cad58cc4d0626d7158299` — the merge of head `a8d843b398bb67c6bbac2719943e599cf8f9b01c` into base `ad632a23a8cadbe8cfae8f1c3fee1052defada29`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1ec515b6b1d6e773119cad58cc4d0626d7158299 && git checkout 1ec515b6b1d6e773119cad58cc4d0626d7158299
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ad632a23a8cadbe8cfae8f1c3fee1052defada29 a8d843b398bb67c6bbac2719943e599cf8f9b01c && git checkout -B drift-repro ad632a23a8cadbe8cfae8f1c3fee1052defada29 && git merge --no-ff a8d843b398bb67c6bbac2719943e599cf8f9b01c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ad632a23a8cadbe8cfae8f1c3fee1052defada29
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

### Contract review brief — PR #37930 @ `a8d843b398bb67c6bbac2719943e599cf8f9b01c` (card #37872)

You review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Render ONE `## Contract review` record on this head — its shape is
`node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --template --paths packages/spec/src/ai/ask-question.zod.ts packages/spec/src/ai/index.ts` — with a PASS or FAIL verdict, and post it as ONE comment
on the PR or its card.

Inputs — these and nothing else:
  · card #37872: its body and EVERY comment (rulings and earlier records included)
  · PR #37930: its body, its file list, and the net diff against `main` at `a8d843b398bb67c6bbac2719943e599cf8f9b01c`
  · the check-runs on `a8d843b398bb67c6bbac2719943e599cf8f9b01c`: their conclusions ARE the gate verdicts
⛔ Not the dispatch order, ⛔ not the dispatching seat's own conclusions — this brief is adversarial by design.

Scope — the paths `reviewFace` returns as `hits` on this PR's file list: packages/spec/src/ai/ask-question.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ai/index.ts;
  plus every file IN THIS DIFF that directly implements or enforces them — the gate that enforces a rule, the code
  a jsdoc or schema line describes, the validator a skill teaches — reviewed for agreement with the contract.
  Widen it freely, ⛔ never below `hits`; the record's `Scope:` line names the implementing files apart from `hits`.
  The rest of the diff (tests, unrelated modules, lockfiles, generated output, changesets) is the lane seat's
  ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, exactly as a standalone PR of those files.
  ④ judges the `hits` files and those implementing files ONLY:
  lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in the PR are not reviewed;
  code outside the diff is READ to judge them, never reviewed.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `SCRATCHPAD/pr-37930/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
     On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
     finding unless a reason is given (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first).
  ④ Design judgment — for EVERY `hits` file: does the change hold against the code it cites and the
     scenario it is accepted against? A skill file against the card's eval prompt and the spec it teaches
     on `main`; a schema file against the ruling or ADR it implements and its first consumer; an ADR
     against its first consumer and its execution plan. For EVERY implementing file in the diff: does the
     code agree with the contract, sentence by sentence? Read the cited code in the live tree, and try to
     break the design.
     Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
     A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
     Spell a must-fix or should-fix with its id and grade, `S1 (should-fix) — …`, and a clean round as
     `No must-fix, no should-fix.`: the queue guard reads a graded finding as OPEN on this head and
     refuses the record; the delta record names those it closes by id alone, `S1: closed`.
     A nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card: a fix
     anywhere else moves the head, and this record no longer covers it.
     ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.
Sign `Implemented-by:` with the dev's branch and `Reviewed-by:` with your session id — the value is the FIRST
thing after each colon.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a8d843b398bb67c6bbac2719943e599cf8f9b01c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/ask-question.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ai/index.ts + packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json

Read, not reviewed: `packages/spec/src/shared/strict-object.ts` and `ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/toolResultParsers.ts` on `main`; `ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/QuestionCard.tsx` at the head of Q2a PR #37932; card #37872 with its two comments; topic #37871; Q2b card #37874. Not readable from this seat: `objectstack-ai/cloud` (the `ask_which` producer, `ask-which.tool.ts`).

Check-runs on this head: 70 in total, 60 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed. Test Core (10 shards), Build Core, TypeScript Type Check, Lint & Repo Gates, Spec property liveness, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Type Check UI and Test UI are all success.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Public surface, added only.** `@objectstack/spec/ai` gains 13 exports: 3 constants (`ASK_QUESTION_LIMITS`, `ASK_QUESTION_STATUS`, `ASK_WHICH_LEGACY_STATUS`), 3 schemas, 6 types (input and `Parsed` pairs) and `parseAskQuestionEnvelope`. `api-surface/ai.json` lists exactly these. Nothing existing is removed, renamed or re-typed. Right.
- **Accept set, new only.** No existing schema's accept set moves. The three new schemas are closed at every level through `strictObject`; the test asserts `unrecognized_keys` at all three levels. Right.
- **Shape and limits against the card.** `success: true`, `status: 'asked'`, `reply` (required, non-empty), `preface?` at most 80, `questions` 1 to 2, `header?` at most 16, `question` at most 120, `options` 2 to 4, `label` at most 24, `description?` at most 60, `recommended?` boolean. Labels are unique within a question and at most one option is recommended, both by `superRefine`. No "type something else" key and no multi-select key. This matches the card's block line by line. Two things go beyond the card and both tighten it: blank strings are refused, and label uniqueness compares trimmed text. Right.
- **Published JSON Schema is wider than the runtime in two places, and both are declared.** The unique-label and single-recommended rules do not project. The two new ledger rows (`ai/AskQuestion` at the root, `ai/AskQuestionEnvelope` at `questions.element`) and the totals (279 to 281 schemas, 1223 to 1225 sites) agree with the one `superRefine` and its one embedding. `AskQuestionOption` has no refinement and correctly has no row. Right.
- **Legacy accept set.** A value with `status: 'asked_which'` is read through an unexported loose object (`success: true`, `question`, `readings: string[]`, `reply`; other keys ignored), converted, and then parsed by the same `AskQuestionEnvelopeSchema`. So a legacy result with 1 reading, 5 or more readings, a duplicate or blank reading, a reading over 24, a question over 120 or an empty reply answers `null`. The tests cover count, duplicate and length. Right as built; see ③ E1 for what it rests on.
- **Authorable surface.** `authorable-surface/ai.json` gains 11 rows for a tool-result shape nobody authors as metadata. The repo's instrument classifies every published schema this way, and `Spec property liveness` is green, so this is consistent with the instrument, and it is what makes `Metadata-protocol: added` the matching kind.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` minor, `Clause-②: yes`, `Metadata-protocol: added`, present and identical in the PR body and the changeset. The diff publishes new exports and three new JSON Schemas and removes nothing, so no BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 disposition is owed. The kind `added` takes at least minor; minor is right. The card orders this same level and kind. `Check Changeset` is success.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag, `out_of_scope_findings`: legacy readings over 24 characters or more than 4 entries answer `null`; cloud reading lengths not measured.** Not answerable from this seat: the cloud repository cannot be read here. **Escalated as E1** to seat `epic:#5027#1`, which owns the cloud side and filed the card with the `ask-which.tool.ts` citation. The question to answer with a measurement: what does `ask_which` allow and typically produce for the number of readings and the length of each reading and of the question? This decides how many of today's ambiguity questions get a card in stage 1 (topic acceptance 1). It does not decide this PR: the envelope schema is the same either way, the failure direction is the text the user sees today (topic acceptance 6 holds), and loosening only the legacy arm later is an additive change to one function. It must be answered before Q2b #37874 claims topic acceptance 1.
- **Dev flag, PR acceptance notes: `Metadata-protocol: added` for a wire shape.** Answered in ① and ②: consistent with the instrument and with the card.
- **Dev flag, PR acceptance notes: a parse helper in `packages/spec`.** Answered: the card orders it there, and `parseFilterAST` and `parseDateMacroParam` on `main` are the precedent. It holds no state and no I/O.
- **Legacy reading against Prime Directive 12.** The legacy arm is a tolerated second shape. It is not a consumer-side fallback: it is declared once in the contract package, tested, held to the contract's limits, and ordered by the card (item 2) under topic decision D1 ("no rewrite of stored tool results"). It reads a tool result, not authored metadata, so no ADR-0087 entry is owed. Answered.
- `open_questions`: empty in the dev report. Nothing to answer.
- SQL push-down: the diff holds no query, no id materialisation and no join. Not applicable.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**`packages/spec/src/ai/ask-question.zod.ts`** against card #37872, topic decisions D1 and D2, and its first consumer (Q2a PR #37932).

- The schema implements the card exactly (① above). Tried to break it: an unknown key at any level, 0 or 3 questions, 1 or 5 options, each length at max plus one, a blank question, an empty label, a trailing-space duplicate label, two recommended, the un-peeled `{ type: 'text', value }` wrapper, arrays and primitives. All are refused or answer `null`, with a test for each.
- First consumer. Q2a's local `QuestionCardQuestion` (`header?`, `question`, `options: readonly QuestionCardOption[]`) and `QuestionCardOption` (`label`, `description?`, `recommended?`) are structurally what `AskQuestionParsed` and `AskQuestionOptionParsed` are; `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` is not set anywhere in the repo, so `parsed.questions` is assignable to the card's `questions` prop without a cast. The card keys options with the digits 1 to 4, which agrees with `maxOptions: 4`; it composes a two-question answer as `header: answer` and falls back to the question text when `header` is absent, which agrees with `header` being optional. `preface` has no reader in Q2a; Q2b step 5 names its reader (the in-thread message) and Q3 its producer. Compatible.
- Holding the legacy reading to the same limits is the sound structure: one contract, one exported type whose limits the card component can rely on, and a safe fallback. Whether it yields enough cards in stage 1 is E1.
- N1 (nit) — three sentences describe readers and producers that do not exist on this head. (a) The `reply` describe, which ships in the package, the JSON Schema and the reference page: "The console draws the card only when this equals the last assistant text". No console code compares `reply` today. The sentence is not false (the console draws no card at all), and it is rule 3 of Q2b #37874 word for word in substance, so it is a commitment Q2b must keep. (b) The module JSDoc says the console "hands the object to `parseAskQuestionEnvelope`"; nothing calls it yet. (c) The `ASK_QUESTION_LIMITS` JSDoc says "the card component lays out against them"; Q2a does not import the limits and hard-codes its four digit keys. Accepted deviation: Q2b #37874 makes (a) and (b) true and must change the describe in its own PR if its rule 3 changes; the changeset already says nothing produces or reads the envelope yet.
- N2 (nit) — the `label` describe says it is "the answer text sent when it is picked". That is exact for one question; for two, the card sends `header: label` lines. Also, uniqueness compares trimmed labels but the stored value is not trimmed, so a label with leading or trailing spaces is accepted and sent as written, and `reply` accepts a whitespace-only string while every other text refuses one. Left as written; a producer-side matter for Q3.
- N3 (nit) — alias tables. They are sensible and collide with no declared key. Three small gaps: the envelope's `question` to `questions` row is one edit away, so the distance fallback already answers it; the two exclusions the JSDoc names (multi-select, and an "other" option) have no `guidance` row, although those are the keys a producer is most likely to try and the ones a rename hint cannot explain; a legacy-shaped `readings` at envelope level gets no pointer. The messages reach only a producer that calls the schema itself, since `parseAskQuestionEnvelope` answers `null` without the issue. Follow-up material for Q3, where the producer is written.

**`packages/spec/src/ai/index.ts`**: one `export *` line and one docblock line. The docblock line ("the envelope a question tool's result carries, from which the console draws a question card") carries the same forward tense as N1 and is covered by it. No name collision in `api-surface/ai.json`.

**`packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`** (implementing): the rows and totals agree with the code (①). N4 (nit) — the two rows sit between `ai/Agent` and `ai/AiContext`, out of the file's alphabetical order; the build accepts it. Left as is.

### ⛔ merge queue 构建失败 — 先分诊，再决定要不要重排

队列构建 [46003823620](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/46003823620) 红了。队列跑的是**全量**套件（PR 侧 CI 只跑 affected 子集），
所以失败的测试可能在本 PR 没碰过的包里 —— 那不是重排能修的。每次盲目重排都会让排在后面的所有 PR 重建一轮。

**分类：`failure`** —— 按下面的日志分诊。

**失败的 job（日志抽取，best effort）：**

- **[Test Core (6/10)](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/46003823620/job/140523275356)** — 失败步骤: Run this shard's tests

  ```
  @objectstack/lint:test:  FAIL  src/authored-site-expression.test.ts > sharedValidatorRunByCaller reaches no gate run (#32872) > is spelled in code only where it is declared, read, and passed by this e
    ↳ 失败原因: @objectstack/lint:test: Error: Test timed out in 5000ms.
  ```

> `↳ 失败原因` 是判读的关键：**超时**（`Test timed out in …` / `Hook timed out in …`）多半是负载/时序，不是本 PR 的回归；
> **断言**（`AssertionError: …`）才指向真实的行为改变。两者的 `FAIL` 行长得一模一样，只有这一行能区分。
>
> ⚠️ **断言这一侧有一类例外，判据是断言在测什么，不是它是不是 `AssertionError`。** 断言的对象是**产品行为**（一个值、一个形状、一次拒收）⇒ 照上面读：真实的行为改变，去查，⛔ 不要重排掉；
> 断言的对象是**这次实验自身的有效性前提**（跑完的耗时、负载下的先后、任何只在时间预算内才成立的条件）⇒ 它跟**超时**是同一类，同样对负载敏感，重排一次是合法的判别手段。
> 识别是机械的：断言的消息或它比较的值本身点名了一段**时长、一个时间戳、一个耗时计数**。实测过的一对 —— `AssertionError: SecurityPlugin.init() ran: expected false to be true` 测的是产品行为（真回归）；
> `AssertionError: this run took over a second, so second-precision stamps could have differed too: expected 1006 to be less than 1000` 测的是实验前提：它守护的那条不变式当时是绿的，同一个 head 原样重排一次即成功。
> 穿着 `AssertionError` 外衣的时间测量，仍然是时间测量。（⛔ 这只改「怎么读一次红」，不改「哪些测试可以重排」——后者由别处管。）
